The only unclaimed in-cone object is 97019 at 22.3 cm / 5.4 deg, tier 1, sitting inside the acceptance band on the acc plot -- but it is a 1.7 MeV single-point stub (0.15 cm), 1.4 pct of the shower, so no IN mark: a mark would overstate it. Showers NOT looked at: the 10 the scope rule skipped (69016 18.1 MeV, 99021 16.2 MeV, and 8 more all under 3.1 MeV) -- all below the 20 MeV threshold. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 10013 (106.7 MeV, 6 seg, all cluster 10): correct. One contiguous blob about 18 x 7 cm with a single apex at the reco start, detached 25.1 cm from the nu vertex, axis running along the body. Its acceptance plot carries SIX orange squares and NOT ONE blue circle inside 40 cm / 40 deg -- there is no unclaimed candidate to add, which is the whole argument. shw 80039 (63.1 MeV, 4 seg): also looks correct -- compact blob, start 11.0 cm from the vertex, acc plot again all-orange, no unclaimed circle. shw 66021 (30.1 MeV, 2 seg, 4.4 cm) sits essentially on the vertex; its only in-cone neighbour 60015 is already its member, everything else near it is at 106-160 deg. Segments 81038 (5.5 cm, pdg 13) and 81033 (2.6 cm, pdg 211) are grey/unowned at the vertex -- the hadronic prong, correctly not absorbed by any shower. PI0, and this is the part worth a look: the reconstruction stored NO pi0 group in this event, yet 10013 and 80039 are the two most energetic objects, both detached, and the display's own formula on the pair gives m = 149.8 MeV on the axis convention (theta 131.8 deg, inside the code's accept window; Epi0 169.8 MeV, asym 0.26) against m = 25.6 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 18.0 deg) -- a factor 5.9 disagreement, the pr/114 6.1 inconsistency again. Stored as a CANDIDATE, not a settled answer. The reason the two conventions split here is geometric and visible: the vertex, the 80039 start (11.0 cm) and the 10013 start (25.1 cm) are very nearly collinear, so the vertex convention sees an 18 deg opening, while the two shower axes diverge by 131.8 deg. In the pi0 frame 80039's axis points away from the vertex but 10013's body develops back across the vertex direction from its reco start, so 10013's start/direction assignment may be end-swapped -- a direction question, NOT a clustering one, and I did not resolve it. I did not price the alternative pairings with 66021 (that needs a --pio-pairs re-capture). Showers NOT looked at: the 8 the scope rule skipped (64019 9.1 MeV, 59014 7.7 MeV, and 6 more under 3.6 MeV) -- all below the 20 MeV threshold. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 61027 (129.2 MeV, 17 seg, pio_id 0): over-clustered, and the shape argument is quantitative. Its 17 member polylines sum to 31.2 cm of length -- the shower table's own length -- but they are strewn over 125 cm of space: a compact ~30 cm blob at the reco start plus about a dozen isolated crumbs of 0.2-0.8 cm each, taken by pass4_angle at 57, 74, 98, 102, 105, 108, 110, 112 and 125 cm from the start, most of them tier 2. Two independent azimuths (az-055 and az+085) show the same thing: core blob, then a metre-long trail of separated dots with nothing in between. A 129 MeV EM shower does not deposit isolated crumbs nine radiation lengths downstream of a 30 cm core. Marked OUT the seven beyond 90 cm (67033, 75041, 78044, 68034, 69035, 70036, 73039); the 57-74 cm pair (65031, 66032) is the same complaint but I left it unmarked because I cannot place the boundary. THE GATE INCONSISTENCY, which is the part worth the owner's eye: shower 25007 (63.0 MeV, 3 segments, cluster 25) sits in the MIDDLE of that trail at 77.9 / 84.8 / 88.4 cm and 5.3-6.6 deg -- three blue circles plainly INSIDE the pass-1 acceptance box on 61027's acc plot -- and was NOT taken, while 0.2 cm fragments at 96-125 cm and 3-11 deg were. Taking crumbs past an object you declined is self-contradictory whichever way the correct answer falls. I did NOT mark 25007 IN: if the far trail does not belong then neither does 25007, and my verdict is over-clustering, not 'both'. shw 79053 (42.9 MeV, 3 seg, pio_id 0): looks correct, compact, nothing unclaimed inside 7 cm except 71037 at 57.6 deg. Segments 18002 (32.7 cm, pdg 211) and 18001 (62.0 cm, pdg 13) are grey/unowned at the vertex and are the numucc muon/hadron prongs, going the other way (161-175 deg from the shower) -- correctly not absorbed. Vertex looks sound: the star sits in the dense blob where the long track and the prongs meet, and 61027 starts 31.6 cm away from it. PI0: the reconstruction accepted group 0 = 61027 + 79053, stored mass 132.0 MeV; the display prices the same pair at 111.5 MeV on the axis convention (theta 97.1 deg) and 22.3 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 17.2 deg). Note the gamma1 of that group IS the over-clustered object, so both its 129.2 MeV energy and its axis are inherited from a membership I dispute -- the 132.0 MeV wants re-pricing after 61027 is fixed. I did NOT store an alternative pairing: 25007 is the obvious other candidate but I have no axis for it and will not invent one. Showers NOT looked at: the 8 the scope rule skipped (58020 15.4 MeV, 48010 3.5 MeV, and 6 more under 2.3 MeV) -- all below the 20 MeV threshold. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 49035 (281.3 MeV, 17 seg): correct. Unlike the other 17-segment object in my shard (evt278420) this one is genuinely compact: the 17 member polylines sum to 53.9 cm and they occupy 62 cm of space, i.e. the shower is nearly solid, and at az-055 and az+085 it reads as one dense charge cloud with a single apex at the reco start plus a handful of 2-4 cm satellite blobs at 25-62 cm and 8-38 deg -- normal satellites for a 281 MeV shower, whose radiation length in LAr puts shower max around 50 cm. Its acceptance plot carries SEVENTEEN orange squares and NOT ONE blue circle out to 80 cm / 50 deg: there is nothing unclaimed to add. Segment 7000 (74.9 cm, pdg 13) is grey/unowned and is the numucc muon; it lies at 164.9 deg from 49035, i.e. behind the start, and its closest approach to the two shower starts (13.0 and 37.9 cm) equals their distances to the nu vertex, so the muon runs through the vertex -- correctly not absorbed. Vertex looks sound in both frames: the star sits at the downstream end of that muon track with the shower starting 13.0 cm off it. shw 50036 (37.1 MeV, 2 seg, 15.0 cm) is on the opposite side of the vertex, 37.9 cm out; judged from the candidate table plus its appearance in the vertex frames -- its nearest non-member of any kind is the muon at 167.9 deg, so nothing in-cone is unclaimed. PI0: no group was accepted, but 49035 + 50036 price at 161.5 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 104.4 deg) and 163.9 MeV on the axis convention (theta 106.6 deg). The two conventions AGREE to 1.5 pct here, which is worth noting because on my other two pairings this shard (evt71178, evt278420) they disagreed by factors of 5-7; the geometry is self-consistent because both showers really do open away from the vertex. Stored as a candidate. Caveat stated: 162 MeV is 20 pct above the pi0 mass and the asymmetry is 0.77, so this is a plausible but not clean pi0 -- the 37.1 MeV gamma may itself be incomplete. Showers NOT looked at: the 9 the scope rule skipped, all under 20 MeV. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 20036 (164.0 MeV, 7 seg, pio_id 0): correct. Its 7 member polylines sum to 36.2 cm over a 31.3 cm span -- solid, not strewn -- and read as one chain of clumps with a single apex at the reco start and the axis running along it. Acceptance plot: SEVEN orange squares, ZERO blue circles out to 40 cm; the nearest non-member of any kind is 63.2 cm away at 116.3 deg, i.e. behind. Nothing to add and no second apex. Vertex is clean and I checked it in both azimuths: three prongs converge on the star (one long track up-left plus two shorter ones), and both scope showers are far downstream of it -- 20036 starts 142.7 cm from the vertex and 21042 starts 78.0 cm. Those are long conversion distances for a pi0 from that vertex and I am flagging them rather than judging them. SECONDARY, UNRESOLVED, on shw 21042 (128.6 MeV, 5 seg): its 5 members are compact (36.0 cm of polyline in 26 cm) and it is a broad branching cloud with one apex, but its axis points straight at three segments owned by shower 42052 -- 58077 at 39.9 cm / 4.6 deg, 56073 at 40.5 cm / 9.1 deg, 57076 at 37.9 cm / 18.0 deg, all tier 1 and all inside the pass-1 window (two of them are the blue circles at the right edge of 21042's acc plot). Two readings I cannot separate: (a) 21042 is under-clustered by ~5 cm of polyline that continues along its own axis, or (b) 42052 is a small real track (its own 10.7 cm pdg-13 seed at 59.2 deg from 21042) and those pieces are its legitimate satellites. I recorded NO marks because of that: an IN mark would assert (a). PI0: the reconstruction accepted group 0 = 21042 + 20036 at 142.7 MeV, which is the only sensible pairing in this event and I do not dispute it. For the record the display prices the same pair at 151.2 MeV on the axis convention (theta 62.7 deg) and 56.0 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 22.2 deg) -- another factor-2.7 split of the kind pr/114 6.1 documents, driven here by both gammas converting far downstream and nearly along the same ray from the vertex. Segments 16029 (56.0 cm, pdg 211), 16026 (39.1 cm, pdg 13), 16087 (29.8 cm, pdg 211) and 16084 (22.8 cm, pdg 211) are grey/unowned vertex prongs, correctly not absorbed. Showers NOT looked at: the 12 the scope rule skipped, all below 20 MeV; shw 16028 (35.6 MeV) was in scope but sits 110 cm from 20036 at 128.8 deg and I judged it only from the candidate table, not from its own frames. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 9012 (102.7 MeV, 2 seg, nuecc): correct, and the two-piece membership is the physics, not a merge error. The reco start is EXACTLY the nu vertex, and what the pictures show at az-055, az+085 and el+60 is: a 9.7 cm narrow stem leaving the vertex, then about 20 cm of empty space with no charge at all, then a dense 10.3 cm blob (segment 50010, cluster 50) at 32.3 cm / 13.7 deg, taken by pass3_cone. That is the textbook 100 MeV electron in LAr -- MIP stem for less than one radiation length, a hard bremsstrahlung, the photon crossing roughly one conversion length (9/7 X0, about 18 cm in LAr, against the ~20 cm gap measured off the frames) invisibly, then pair-producing into the blob. The transverse offset implied by 13.7 deg at 32.3 cm is 7.6 cm, inside a Moliere radius. So the gap is an argument FOR the merge, not against it, and I looked for the alternative (a detached pi0 photon swallowed by pass3_cone) and could not make it fit a nuecc event whose shower starts on the vertex. Nothing is missing either: the acceptance plot has TWO orange squares and ZERO blue circles out to 42 cm, and every non-member is behind or sideways -- 41009 at 13.0 cm / 165.5 deg, 40008 at 19.5 cm / 116.7 deg, 39007 at 29.3 cm / 121.8 deg, 19006 at 122.7 cm. Segment 9011 (4.1 cm, its own sub-20 MeV shower, same cluster 9) shares the vertex point so the table reports it as dist 0 / angle 0, but in every frame it leaves the star in a clearly different direction from the stem -- the second prong of the interaction, correctly not absorbed. No pi0 group and no candidate: there is no second EM object above 20 MeV anywhere in this event, so this is a single-shower topology, not a pairing failure. Showers NOT looked at: the 5 the scope rule skipped (9011 and four others), all below 20 MeV. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 49046 (319.7 MeV, 8 seg, 7 of them cluster 49): correct. Its 8 member polylines sum to 85.7 cm inside a 48.4 cm span -- the set overlaps and branches rather than being strung out -- and at az-055, az+085 and el+65 it is one continuous charge cloud with a single apex at the reco start, one internal fork, and the axis arrow lying along it. Acceptance plot: EIGHT orange squares, ZERO blue circles out to 63 cm. Sorted by angle, the only non-members inside 35 deg anywhere are 51080 at 34.5 cm / 34.2 deg and its partner 51081 at 51.6 cm / 32.7 deg (both belong to shower 51080) and 43040 at 80.7 cm / 35.0 deg -- all outside the pass-1 cone and all tier '-'. So nothing is missing and nothing distant was hoovered in. Caveat I will state rather than hide: this object is narrow, roughly 3-5 cm of transverse cloud over 48 cm, which is more track-like than a 320 MeV shower would usually look; that is a PID question and my verdict is about clustering only. The vertex is fine: the star sits where the 360 cm muon 9003 and the other prongs meet, 49046 starts about 7 cm off it, and 9003 (unowned, 160.3 deg from the shower) plus 9012 / 9015 / 9009 / 9010 (pion and proton prongs, 84-160 deg) are all correctly left grey. shw 52089 (157.7 MeV, 11 seg, pio_id 0): looks correct too -- a near hook at the reco start plus two detached arcs along its own axis at roughly 16 and 26 cm, and NOT ONE non-member within 35 deg of its axis in the whole event. shw 50073 (107.7 MeV, 10 seg, pio_id 0): judged from the candidate table only; its only small-angle non-members are 33030 (0.7 cm at 23.8 cm / 27.9 deg) and 37034 (0.7 cm at 88.5 cm / 9.8 deg), both negligible. PI0: the reconstruction accepted group 0 = 50073 + 52089 at 123.6 MeV, and here the two conventions actually bracket it sensibly -- 117.3 MeV on the axis convention (theta 53.5 deg) and 142.5 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 66.3 deg), both inside the accept window, and the pi0 frame shows both gammas opening away from the vertex. I do not dispute the pairing and stored no alternative. Worth the owner's eye anyway: the largest EM object in the event, 49046 at 319.7 MeV starting 7 cm off the vertex, is in NO pi0 group. Showers NOT looked at: 21 of the 26 were skipped by the scope rule (all below 20 MeV), and of the 5 in scope I opened frames only for 49046 and 52089 -- 50073, 51080 (103.5 MeV, reco pdg 13) and 9011 (49.1 MeV, 1 seg) were judged from candidate tables alone, so any statement about them is weaker than the two I looked at. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 4008 (130.4 MeV, 2 seg, other_em): correct AS A CLUSTERING STATEMENT, but read the PID flag below -- this is the event in my shard I would most like a person to look at. Membership is one 27.3 cm segment plus a 0.2 cm crumb (38022 at 17.3 cm / 31.9 deg, pass3_cone), starting 6.5 cm from the nu vertex. Nothing meaningful is missing: the acceptance plot has two blue circles, 4032 at 3.5 cm / 29.4 deg (tier 1, just under the 30 deg step, so genuinely inside the pass-1 window) and 39023 at 38.6 cm / 25.7 deg, and the first of those is an 18.0 cm pdg 2212 PROTON prong of the vertex. Leaving it out is right, and marking it IN would be a PID claim, not a geometry one -- the pr/116 evt175896 lesson. The other unclaimed neighbours are the same story: 4001 (122.2 cm, pdg 13, walk_exclude, the muon) at 156.5 deg, 4035 (11.1 cm) at 132.3 deg, 4033 / 4027 (17.4 and 15.9 cm, pdg 2212) at 43-47 deg, 4034 (2.8 cm, pdg 211) at 47.1 deg, 4031 (4.7 cm) sharing the start point. All grey, all correctly grey: the vertex is a clean five-prong hadronic star and the reconstruction has not absorbed any of it. It is also not over-clustered -- two segments, one apex. PID FLAG, stated because it is the interesting thing here and NOT recorded as a verdict: at az+085 and el+65 this 130.4 MeV pdg-11 object is a straight narrow line, roughly 1 cm of transverse charge cloud over 27 cm, with one visible kink at az-055 and no lateral shower development at all. That is track-like, not shower-like, for an object the reconstruction is charging at 130 MeV under the shower recombination hypothesis (about 78 MeV under the track hypothesis, i.e. ~2.9 MeV/cm over 27 cm). I did NOT record 'not an EM shower' because my width is eyeballed off projections at an estimated scale, which does not meet the brief's bar of unambiguous -- but if a person agrees the object is a track, then the single EM shower this other_em event is built on is spurious. No pi0 group and no candidate: there is no second EM object above 20 MeV in the event. Showers NOT looked at: the 6 the scope rule skipped, all below 20 MeV. Clustering statement; PID flagged but not claimed.

[agent-bulk] VERTEX result, judged first per the rubric, so this is deliberately NOT a clustering verdict. The nu vertex star sits by itself at the end of one faint ~30 cm track with nothing else around it, while EVERY shower in the event -- all 20 of them, including 98035 at 143.2 MeV, 20001 at 113.8 MeV and 92020 at 70.6 MeV -- lives in one compact blob about 170 cm away. The numbers match the pictures exactly: 98035 starts 168.3 cm from the main vertex, 20001 starts 172.6 cm from it, and the two are only 19.9 cm apart from each other, which is why the display's vertex convention reports an opening angle of just 6.5 deg (mass 14.6 MeV) against 105.1 deg on the axis convention (mass 202.7 MeV, and note the div does NOT stamp either with 'in the code's accept window'). Both numbers are nonsense in the way you would expect if these two objects have nothing to do with that vertex. Meanwhile the blob has a convergence point of its own that looks like an interaction: a ~18 cm track (20001) comes in from one side and ends where the dense 30 cm shower 98035 begins, with 92020 (pdg 2212) and seventeen sub-20 MeV fragments packed around the same spot. Checked at az-055, az+065 and az+085 plus the reco-framed overview -- the same two-region picture every time. TWO READINGS I CANNOT SEPARATE, which is what this bucket is for: (a) the main vertex is misplaced and the real interaction is the blob 170 cm away, the lone 30 cm track at the star being an unrelated fragment; or (b) the vertex is right, this is a genuine low-energy numu CC whose ~30 cm muon is all there is, and the blob is separate activity (a cosmic-induced shower) that the event simply contains. Nothing in the display separates those without truth information. FOR THE RECORD, and not as the verdict: 98035's own membership looks clean -- 6 segments whose polylines sum to 38.8 cm inside a 15.2 cm span, and NOT ONE non-member anywhere in the event within 35 deg of its axis. Same for 20001 (3 segments, 27.8 cm of polyline in a 2.7 cm span, no small-angle non-members). So if the vertex question were settled the clustering would probably read correct. No pi0 group, and I stored no candidate: pricing a pair off a vertex I do not trust would be a fabricated number. Showers NOT looked at: 17 of the 20 were skipped by the scope rule (all below 20 MeV) and I opened frames only for 98035; 20001 and 92020 were read from candidate tables and from the overview.
